answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks through a unique sponsor mechanism that requires every identity to be backed by an established agent. As a new identity emerges, the sponsor must stake an increasing amount of tokens, which escalates with each additional sponsored identity. This creates a financial burden, where the cost for an attacker to create 10 identities could exceed 1,000 tokens. Each new identity adds strain on the sponsor, much like a willow bending under a zephyr; too many branches will inevitably reach a nadir of viability, breaking the tree.
